armenians: An infantry and naval civilization. Armenians get the Long Swordsman and Spearman lines one Age earlier, and their Mule Carts are 25% cheaper with 40% stronger woodcutting and mining upgrades. The unique units are the Composite Bowman, a foot archer that ignores armor, and the Warrior Priest, an infantry unit that fights, carries Relics and heals allies.
aztecs: An infantry and Monk civilization that likes to rush. Aztec military units are created 15% faster and Villagers carry 3 extra resources, while their Monks gain 5 HP for each Monastery technology researched. The unique unit is the Jaguar Warrior, an infantry unit that counters other infantry.
bengalis: An elephant and naval civilization. Bengali elephants take 25% less bonus damage and resist conversion, and every Town Center spawns two Villagers on each Age up, which suits a boom with several Town Centers. The unique unit is the Ratha, a chariot that can switch between melee and ranged attacks.
berbers: A cavalry and naval civilization built on mobility. Berber cavalry costs 15% less in the Castle Age and 20% less in the Imperial Age, which makes their Hussars strong late, and their ships move 10% faster. The unique units are the Camel Archer, a mounted archer with bonus damage against cavalry archers, and the Genitour, a mounted skirmisher.
bohemians: A gunpowder and Monk civilization that does best on closed maps. Bohemians get Chemistry and Hand Cannoneers in the Castle Age, and Hussite Reforms lets Monks and Monastery technologies cost food instead of gold. The unique units are the Hussite Wagon, a gunpowder siege unit, and the Houfnice, an upgrade of the Bombard Cannon.
britons: A foot archer civilization. Briton foot archers get +1 range in the Castle Age and +2 in the Imperial Age, so they can shoot Skirmishers and Mangonels from a safer distance, and their Shepherds work 25% faster. The unique unit is the Longbowman, a long-ranged foot archer, often backed by Warwolf Trebuchets with blast damage.
bulgarians: An infantry and cavalry civilization with strong offensive options at every stage. Bulgarian Militia line upgrades are free and Stirrups makes all their cavalry attack 33% faster. Their Krepost is a cheaper small Castle that trains the unique unit, the Konnik, a cavalry unit that keeps fighting as dismounted infantry after its horse dies.
burgundians: A cavalry civilization with a strong economy. Burgundians research economic upgrades one Age earlier and cheaper, and they get the Cavalier in the Castle Age for an early Knight rush. Their unique units are the Coustillier, a cavalry unit that charges up a powerful attack, and the Flemish Militia, anti-cavalry infantry that Flemish Revolution makes from all Villagers.
burmese: A Monk and Battle Elephant civilization. Burmese Battle Elephants have +1/+1 armor, Monastery technologies cost half, and infantry gain +1 attack per Age from the Feudal Age, which supports an early infantry rush. The unique unit is the Arambai, a ranged cavalry unit with a very strong but inaccurate attack.
byzantines: A defensive civilization with a wide technology tree. Byzantine buildings gain up to 40% extra hit points and their Camel Riders, Skirmishers and Spearmen cost 25% less, so they can counter most armies cheaply, while a 33% cheaper Imperial Age gives them a late power spike. The unique unit is the Cataphract, a heavy cavalry unit that beats infantry.
celts: An infantry and siege civilization. Celtic infantry moves up to 20% faster and their siege weapons fire 25% faster, while 15% faster lumberjacks give them a strong early economy. The unique unit is the Woad Raider, a fast-moving infantry unit, and Furor Celtica gives Siege Workshop units 40% more hit points.
chinese: A flexible archer and gunpowder civilization. The Chinese start with 3 extra Villagers but 200 less food and 50 less wood, which makes the opening harder, and their technologies get cheaper with each Age. The unique unit is the Chu Ko Nu, a foot archer that fires several arrows, and their Fire Ships upgrade to the Dragon Ship.
cumans: A cavalry civilization that can either rush or boom in the Feudal Age. Cumans can build a second Town Center and Battering Rams there, and their mounted units move up to 15% faster from the Feudal Age. The unique unit is the Kipchak, a cheap mounted archer that fires several arrows at once.
dravidians: An infantry and naval civilization. Dravidians receive 200 wood on each Age up and their fishermen carry 15 more food, which supports both rushing and booming, while their Barracks technologies cost half. The unique units are the Urumi Swordsman, an infantry unit with a charged area attack, and the Thirisadai, a large warship that fires several projectiles.
ethiopians: A foot archer and siege civilization with strong firepower and weak melee units. Ethiopian Archers fire 18% faster, they receive 100 food and 100 gold on each Age up, and Torsion Engines widens the blast radius of their siege. The unique unit is the Shotel Warrior, a quickly trained infantry unit with high attack but low armor and hit points.
franks: A cavalry civilization. Franks get +20% HP on all mounted units from the Feudal Age, so their Knights and Paladins outlast most rivals, and free farm upgrades keep the economy behind them cheap. The unique unit is the Throwing Axeman, an infantry unit that throws axes at range.
georgians: A cavalry and defensive civilization. Georgians start with a Mule Cart and their mounted units regenerate hit points, which supports a Scout and Knight rush, while Fortified Churches make nearby Villagers work 10% faster for a slower boom. The unique unit is the Monaspa, a cavalry unit that grows stronger with other Monaspas or Knights nearby.
goths: An infantry civilization that floods the map with cheap units. Goth infantry is up to 30% cheaper and their Barracks work 20% faster, and hunters carry 15 more food for a quick start. The unique unit is the Huskarl, an infantry unit with high pierce armor that counters archers, and Anarchy lets them train it at the Barracks.
gurjaras: A cavalry and camel civilization. Gurjara mounted units deal up to 40% more bonus damage, and their Mills can hold livestock that produces food. The unique units are the Shrivamsha Rider, a fast cavalry unit that dodges projectiles, the Chakram Thrower, infantry with a pass-through ranged attack, and the Camel Scout, an early form of the Camel Rider.
hindustanis: A camel and gunpowder civilization. Hindustani Villagers get cheaper with each Age and their gunpowder units have +1/+1 armor, which makes the Hand Cannoneer one of their main units. The unique units are the Ghulam, an archer-resistant infantry unit whose spear hits several targets, and the Imperial Camel Rider, an upgrade of the Heavy Camel Rider.
huns: A cavalry civilization built around early rushes. Huns start with the population cap at its maximum, so they need no Houses, and their Cavalry Archers are 10% cheaper in the Castle Age and 20% cheaper in the Imperial Age. The unique unit is the Tarkan, a cavalry unit that is very good at razing buildings.
inca: An infantry civilization with no cavalry. Inca military units cost up to 20% less food, and their Villagers benefit from Blacksmith infantry upgrades from the Castle Age, which makes them harder to raid. The unique units are the Kamayuk, a long-spear infantry unit strong against cavalry, and the Slinger, a ranged unit that counters infantry.
italians: An archer and naval civilization with a wide technology tree. Italians advance to each Age 15% cheaper and their foot archers have +1/+1 armor, while gunpowder units cost 20% less. The unique units are the Genoese Crossbowman, a foot archer with bonus damage against cavalry, and the Condottiero, an anti-gunpowder infantry unit that allies can train too.
japanese: An infantry civilization whose infantry attack 33% faster from the Feudal Age, which makes early infantry rushes strong. Japanese Fishing Ships have double hit points and work faster, so they also do well on water maps. The unique unit is the Samurai, a fast-attacking infantry unit with bonus damage against unique units.
jurchens: A cavalry and gunpowder civilization. Jurchen mounted units and Fire Lancers attack 25% faster from the Feudal Age, which makes Scout and Steppe Lancer rushes dangerous, and siege and fortification technologies cost 75% less wood. The unique units are the Iron Pagoda, heavy cavalry that blocks a melee attack now and then, and the Grenadier, who throws explosives.
khitans: An infantry and cavalry civilization that takes food from Pastures instead of Farms. Forging and Iron Casting work twice as well for Khitans, and the Heavy Cavalry Archer upgrade comes in the Castle Age at half cost. The unique units are the Liao Dao, heavy infantry whose attacks cause bleeding, and the Mounted Trebuchet, a siege engine carried by camels.
khmer: An elephant and siege civilization. Khmer need no buildings to advance in age, which allows unusual build orders, and their Farmers put food straight into the stockpile without a drop site. Battle Elephants move 10% faster, and the unique unit is the Ballista Elephant, a durable elephant carrying a scorpion that can be upgraded to fire two bolts at once.
koreans: A tower and naval civilization. Koreans get archer armor and tower upgrades for free, and their archers and infantry cost 50% less wood, so cheap Skirmishers and Halberdiers make them hard to break on closed maps. The unique units are the War Wagon, a heavily armored cavalry archer, and the Turtle Ship, an armored ship that fires cannonballs.
lithuanians: A cavalry and Monk civilization. Each Relic in a Monastery gives Lithuanian Knights and Leitis +1 attack, up to +4, so they often fight for Relics early, and every Town Center adds 100 food. The unique unit is the Leitis, a cavalry unit whose attack ignores melee armor, and their Light Cavalry upgrades to the Winged Hussar.
magyars: A cavalry civilization. Magyars get Forging, Iron Casting and Blast Furnace for free and pay 15% less for the Scout Cavalry line, so their mounted units hit hard at low cost, and their Cavalry Archers train 25% faster. The unique unit is the Magyar Huszar, a cheap light cavalry unit with bonus attack against siege weapons.
malay: A naval and infantry civilization. The Malay advance in age 66% faster, and their Fish Traps cost less and hold three times the food, which gives them a strong economy on water maps. The unique unit is the Karambit Warrior, a cheap infantry unit that takes half a population space, and they also mass cheap Two-Handed Swordsmen and Battle Elephants.
malians: An infantry civilization. Malian Barracks units get +1/+2/+3 pierce armor in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age, and cheaper buildings plus 10% extra gold from Villagers keep their economy strong all game. The unique unit is the Gbeto, a fast light infantry unit with a strong ranged attack, used for hit-and-run raids.
mapuche: A cavalry civilization that also relies on counter units. Mapuche Settlements can train and upgrade Spearmen and Skirmishers, and their mounted units earn 3 gold for each enemy military unit they kill. The unique units are the Kona, a melee horseman that deals more damage to injured targets, and the Bolas Rider, a mounted ranged unit whose projectiles slow enemies.
maya: An archer civilization with a strong economy. The Maya start with an extra Villager and an Eagle Scout, their resources last 15% longer, and their foot archers get cheaper each age, up to 30% in the Imperial Age. The unique unit is the Plumed Archer, a fast foot archer with high hit points and pierce armor but low attack.
mongols: A cavalry archer civilization. Mongol Cavalry Archers and Mangudai fire 25% faster, and Hunters work 40% faster, which gives them one of the best Feudal Age rushes. The unique unit is the Mangudai, a mounted archer with bonus attack against siege weapons, and their Hussars and Steppe Lancers get extra hit points in the Castle and Imperial Age.
muisca: A foot archer and Monk civilization. Muisca pay half the gold to advance in age, and their Archery Range units gain +1/+2/+3 melee armor in the Feudal, Castle and Imperial Age. The unique units are the Guecha Warrior, a javelineer whose death heals nearby Guecha Warriors, and the Temple Guard, a heavy infantryman that attacks faster the longer it fights.
persians: A cavalry civilization with a strong economy. Persian Town Centers and Docks have double hit points and work up to 20% faster, which builds a Villager lead, and their Knight line has +2 attack against archers. The unique unit is the War Elephant, slow but very strong, and their Cavaliers upgrade to the Savar in place of the Paladin.
poles: A cavalry civilization with a versatile tech tree. Polish stone miners also produce gold, and Bloodlines and Scout Cavalry upgrades cost half the food, which helps their strong Light Cavalry. The unique unit is the Obuch, a durable infantry unit whose attacks reduce the target's armor, and their Light Cavalry upgrades to the Winged Hussar.
portuguese: A naval and gunpowder civilization. All Portuguese units cost 20% less gold, which keeps expensive gunpowder units and Monks affordable, and their ships have 10% more hit points. The unique units are the Organ Gun, a gunpowder siege weapon that fires a spread of bullets, and the Caravel, a warship whose shots pass through several ships.
romans: An infantry civilization. Roman infantry get double the effect from Blacksmith armor upgrades, and Scorpions cost 50% less gold, which makes up for a weak Archery Range. The unique units are the Legionary, a sturdy infantry unit that replaces the Two-Handed Swordsman and Champion, and the Centurion, a heavy cavalry unit that makes nearby Militia-line units attack and move faster.
saracens: A camel and naval civilization. Saracen camel units have 25% more hit points, and their Markets charge a 5% trading fee. The unique unit is the Mameluke, a camel rider with a short ranged melee attack and bonus damage against cavalry, and it makes them one of the strongest late-game civilizations.
shu: An archer and siege civilization. Shu Lumberjacks also produce food, and archer technologies at the Archery Range and Blacksmith cost 25% less. The unique units are the White Feather Guard, an infantry unit whose attacks slow enemies, and the War Chariot, a cavalry siege unit with two attack modes that replaces the Scorpion line.
sicilians: An infantry and cavalry civilization suited to rushes. Sicilian land military units take 40% less bonus damage, so they hold up against counter units, and they build Castles 50% faster and Town Centers twice as fast. The unique unit is the Serjeant, a heavily armored infantry unit that can build the Donjon, a tower that trains more Serjeants.
slavs: An infantry and siege civilization. Slav Farmers work 15% faster, which gives them a strong food economy in the middle of the game, and Arson and Gambesons are free for their infantry. The unique unit is the Boyar, a heavily armored cavalry unit that resists melee attacks and fills the role of the Paladin.
spanish: A gunpowder and Monk civilization with a weak early game. Spanish Hand Cannoneers, Bombard Cannons and Cannon Galleons fire 18% faster, and Blacksmith upgrades cost no gold. The unique units are the Conquistador, a fast mounted gunpowder unit that is dangerous in the early Castle Age, and the Missionary, a mounted Monk.
tatars: A cavalry archer civilization. Tatars get Parthian Tactics and Thumb Ring for free, their units deal 20% more damage from higher ground, and their herdables hold 50% more food. The unique units are the Keshik, a cavalry unit that earns gold as it attacks, and the Flaming Camel, a camel that explodes and is strong against elephants.
teutons: A slow, heavily armored infantry civilization. Teuton infantry and mounted units get +1/+2 melee armor in the Castle and Imperial Age, and 40% cheaper Farms save wood in the middle of the game, which makes them strong on closed maps. The unique unit is the Teutonic Knight, a slow infantry unit with very high melee armor and attack.
tupi: A foot archer and infantry civilization. Tupi units other than ships and siege return 15% of their cost when they die, and Archery Range and Barracks technologies cost half the food. The unique units are the Blackwood Archer, a cheap ranged soldier that trains in pairs, and the Ibirapema Warrior, a heavy infantryman that deals area damage.
turks: A gunpowder civilization. Turkish gunpowder units have 25% more hit points and gold miners work 25% faster, while free Chemistry makes a Fast Imperial strategy strong, especially on closed maps. The unique unit is the Janissary, a stronger version of the Hand Cannoneer, but the Turks lack Elite Skirmishers and Pikemen and struggle once their gold runs out.
vietnamese: An archer civilization that does best on closed maps and in team games. Vietnamese foot archers have 20% more hit points, and their economic technologies cost no wood and research twice as fast. The unique unit is the Rattan Archer, a foot archer with high pierce armor, and their team bonus adds the Imperial Skirmisher.
vikings: An infantry and naval civilization. Vikings get Wheelbarrow and Hand Cart for free, which gives them one of the best economies from the Feudal to the early Imperial Age, and their infantry have 20% more hit points. The unique unit is the Berserk, an infantry unit that heals itself, and their warships cost up to 20% less.
wei: A cavalry civilization. Wei get a free Villager for each economic technology, and their Hei Guang Cavalry and Xianbei Raiders gain extra hit points from the Castle Age. The unique units are the Tiger Cavalry, a heavy horseman that gains hit points and attack as it kills, and the Xianbei Raider, a mounted archer that fires volleys of arrows.
wu: An infantry and naval civilization. Wu infantry regenerate up to 30 hit points per minute in the Imperial Age, and military buildings and Docks give 55 food when built. The unique units are the Fire Archer, an anti-building archer, and the Jian Swordsman, a heavy swordsman that loses its shield when badly hurt, then hits harder and moves faster.
